def factor_vol_adaptive_momentum_blend_v2(df):
    df_copy = df.copy()
    returns = df_copy["close"].pct_change()
    vol_short = returns.rolling(5, min_periods=5).std()
    vol_long = returns.rolling(20, min_periods=20).std()
    vol_ratio = vol_short / vol_long.replace(0.0, np.nan)
    vol_rank = vol_ratio.rolling(252, min_periods=20).rank(pct=True)
    mom_short = df_copy["close"] / df_copy["close"].shift(5) - 1
    mom_long = df_copy["close"] / df_copy["close"].shift(20) - 1
    factor = vol_rank * mom_short + (1.0 - vol_rank) * mom_long
    return pd.Series(factor, index=df_copy.index, name="factor_vol_adaptive_momentum_blend_v2")
description: Mutation of factor_vol_adaptive_momentum_blend: instead of blending based on historical percentile of absolute 20-day volatility, this variant uses the historical percentile of the ratio between short-term (5-day) and long-term (20-day) volatility. When short-term volatility spikes relative to long-term volatility, it indicates a turbulent period, and the factor shifts weight toward short-term momentum (5-day) to capture rapid re-pricing; when short-term volatility is low relative to long-term, it emphasizes longer-term momentum (20-day) for stability. This relative volatility regime measure may be more responsive to turning points while preserving the smooth, data-driven blending mechanism.
